title: Hunger Games prequel splits opinion: 'Surreally awful' or 'surprisingly strong'
content:
Reviews of the latest Hunger Games film have seen it dismissed as a "surreally awful prequel" and "a tortuous, costly mess" by some critics - but called "surprisingly strong" and "one of the best films in the series" by others.
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is the sixth movie in the franchise, and tells the origin story of a teenage Haymitch Abernathy - who was played as an adult by Woody Harrelson.
In a one-star review, the Guardian called the film "overwrought and boring", and said it "has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase".
But the Wrap praised its "memorable performances, intoxicating style and horrifying commentary", adding: "When the dust settles it may even be the Hunger Games that holds up best."
Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the first Hunger Games film, and 40 years after the previous prequel, 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.
"This prequel lands at some mid-point between Ballad and Hunger Games, which puts it on an immediately odd footing," Empire said in a three-star review .
"It can't escape the sense of feeling supplementary. It's an enjoyable-enough diversion, but essentially a footnote with aspirations."
Screen Daily called it an "underwhelming prequel", which "suffers from a lack of compelling characters" and "feels oddly incidental - a drab afterthought rather than a crucial new chapter".
The film's all-star cast includes Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace and Maya Hawke alongside Joseph Zada as the 16-year-old Abernathy.
IndieWire said Zada's performance is "charming enough", but "his character lacks the gravitational charisma or arc that, say, Jennifer Lawrence brought to the original films".
The movie feels "a little bit like a cold cash grab rather than a necessary deepening of the series' lore" and is "a dreary slog", IndieWire's critic wrote.
The New York Times also used the word "slog", adding: "One really misses the guiding presence of Jennifer Lawrence, who had the raw pathos to both ground and expand a world in a way many younger stars often can't.
"In Sunrise, we're instead left with fleeting moments in which Plemons or Ralph Fiennes (playing the evil President Snow) briefly elevate the film. They seem to be trapped in this dystopia too."
However, the Hollywood Reporter was more enthusiastic about both the film and Zada's performance, calling it a "star-making turn".
Its critic concluded: "Sunrise on the Reaping is a return, after the disappointing Songbirds and Snakes, to the spirit of the first movies."
And Time Out's four-star review said the film is "as strong as any" of the other movies, and "certainly a major step up from 2023's drab prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes".

final_quality.reason: The article provides a concise summary of the varying opinions on the latest Hunger Games film, featuring a mix of positive and negative reviews from reputable sources. While the opinions are split, the article presents a balanced view of the different perspectives, making it a useful read for fans of the franchise and those interested in entertainment news.

title: 'Look who it isnae' - Still Game set to return as stage show
content:
Seven years ago, Scotland's most beloved pensioners climbed to the top of Ben Lomond and reached the big Clansman in the sky.
But now, Jack Jarvis and Victor McDade have been resurrected as Still Game returns to the stage for a special run of shows.
The stage show, Still Game Live: Heaven Sent, will have a 10-date run at the Ovo Hydro in Glasgow from February 2028.
Creators Ford Kiernan and Greg Hemphill joked they had a "fear of moving on" after announcing the characters' return.
The ninth and final series of the BBC comedy aired in 2019.
However, the last appearance of the duo came in another stage show, Still Game: The Final Farewell, later the same year.
Kiernan and Hemphill previously said the final series and stage show would be the "final nail in the final coffin".
They did adapt the series for a comic book , which was released in 2024.
In a statement, they said: "We had FOMO (Fear of moving on).
"Haud oan! Whit's been happenin? It's been far too lang…Craiglang."
Still Game first arrived on TV screens in 2002, although the characters of Jack and Victor previously featured in sketch show Chewin' the Fat.
Alongside old pals Winston Ingram, played by Paul Riley, tight-fisted Tam Mullen, played by Mark Cox, nosy Isa Drennan, played by Jane McCarry and shop owner Navid Harrid, played by Sanjeev Kohli, the comedy follows the lives of Jack and Victor as they navigate the fictional Glasgow suburb of Craiglang.
The death of most of the characters was teased at the end of the ninth season and confirmed in The Final Farwell.
The stage show centred on Clansman barman Boaby, played by Gavin Mitchell, joining some of the characters in heaven.
It has not been confirmed who will return alongside Jack and Victor for the new show.
The cast previously set a string of box-office records with their hugely popular live shows in 2014, 2017 and 2019.
Tickets go on sale on Friday.

final_quality.reason: The article reports a significant development in the entertainment category, specifically the return of the popular Scottish comedy show Still Game to the stage. The show has a dedicated fan base and its previous live shows have set box-office records. The article provides some context and quotes from the creators, making it a worthwhile read for fans of the show.

title: Major concerts to return to Platt Fields Park
content:
Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner.
The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill.
Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August.
The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks.
Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds.
Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023.
Sam Kandel, founder of The Warehouse Project and an event director, said the park had its "own unique character", shaped by its location and surrounding communities.
Councillor Shazia Butt, Manchester City Council's executive member for culture, leisure and libraries, welcomed the announcement.
She said the council would work closely with organisers to ensure "maximum benefit for Platt Fields and for the local community", with further information expected in the coming months.
Tickets for the LCD Soundsystem concert go on general sale on Friday 20 November.
